prompt.context: Our client is a global pharmaceutical company headquartered in Frankfurt, Germany that produces over-the-counter drugs. The company is thinking of acquiring another pharmaceutical company located in San Francisco that produces nutritional drugs (for weight loss, diabetes, etc.). The CEO hired us to advise whether they should acquire the company or not.
prompt.question: What are the key areas to investigate in order to determine whether the acquisition is a good idea or not?

clarifying_info.q: What is the purpose of the acquisition?
clarifying_info.a: The purpose of the acquisition is to increase profits.

clarifying_info.q: How many drugs does the San Francisco company have on the market?
clarifying_info.a: The San Francisco company has 4 drugs in the market.

clarifying_info.q: Where do the two companies sell their products?
clarifying_info.a: Both companies sell their products globally.

clarifying_info.q: Where is the R&D department located?
clarifying_info.a: The R&D department is co-located with headquarters.

clarifying_info.q: What is the revenue from an approved drug of the target company?
clarifying_info.a: Revenues from an approved drug of the San Francisco-based company is $1.5M.

exhibits.title: Drug Development Pipeline — Phase Yield Rates
exhibits.shows: A pipeline diagram showing the sequential phases of drug development (Phase 1, Phase 2, Phase 3, and Launch) with the yield (success rate) for each phase transition displayed.

framework: Acquisition rationale: understand strategic motivation — acquire resources (capacity, distribution, product line, technology, human capital, R&D, brand name, customer base) or reduce costs (economies of scale, economies of scope)
Economic viability: determine whether the acquisition has a positive NPV
Organizational integration: assess whether potential synergies will be realized and whether the acquirer is positioned to perform the integration
Geographic considerations: assess differences between Frankfurt HQ and San Francisco target (culture, regulation, operations)
Competitive response: evaluate likely competitor reactions if the acquisition occurs
Alternatives: compare acquisition to other options such as targeting a different company or pursuing organic growth

questions.prompt: Question 1: The company just discovered that the yield from Phase 2 to Phase 3 can be improved by investing $150K in R&D technology. By how much should the yield increase so as to break even on the investment?
questions.guidance: Candidate should set up a break-even equation: incremental investment equals incremental revenue from an additional drug reaching market. Incremental revenue is the PV of a launched drug times the increase in Phase 2-to-3 yield times the remaining pipeline yield (Phase 3 to launch: 70% × 90%). Candidate should solve for the required yield increase and then express it as a percentage of the current Phase 2-to-3 yield (40%) to show strategic significance.

math.setup: Break-even condition: incremental cost = incremental revenue. Let x = required increase in Phase 2-to-3 success rate. Incremental revenue = PV of launched drug × x × (yield Phase 3 to Launch) × (Launch approval rate) = $1,500,000 × x × 70% × 90%.
steps: As a share of current Phase 2-to-3 yield: 15.8% / 40% ≈ 40% improvement required
math.answer: The Phase 2-to-3 yield must increase by approximately 15.8 percentage points, which represents roughly a 40% improvement over the current 40% yield.

questions.prompt: Question 2: What are the risks involved with this acquisition?
questions.guidance: Candidate should identify multiple distinct risk categories: strategic rationale risk (does the deal align with long-term strategy?), competitive risk (likely competitor response to the acquisition), organizational/integration risk (different locations — Frankfurt vs. San Francisco — cultural and operational integration challenges), financial risk (whether NPV is positive, whether synergies are achievable), and alternatives risk (whether better options exist such as a different acquisition target or organic growth).

brainstorming.prompt: What are the risks involved with this acquisition?

categories.name: Strategic rationale
ideas: Unclear or weak strategic fit with core OTC business
Nutritional drug segment may not align with long-term corporate strategy

categories.name: Competitive response
ideas: Competitors may accelerate their own acquisitions of similar targets
Competitors may attempt to poach key talent from the target
Market dynamics may shift against the acquirer post-announcement

categories.name: Organizational and integration
ideas: HQ in Frankfurt vs. target in San Francisco — significant geographic and time-zone gap
Cultural differences between German and US corporate environments
R&D co-located with HQ may create friction when integrating San Francisco R&D
Risk of key talent attrition during integration

categories.name: Financial and profitability
ideas: Acquisition may yield negative NPV if synergies are overestimated
Pipeline drugs may fail in later phases, reducing revenue projections
Valuation risk — target may be overpriced

categories.name: Alternatives
ideas: Better acquisition targets may exist in the nutritional drug space
Organic growth in nutritional drugs may be more cost-effective
Licensing or partnership agreements could achieve similar goals without full acquisition

recommendation: Proceed with or reject the acquisition based on NPV analysis — the investment makes sense only if synergies and incremental revenues outweigh the acquisition price and integration costs

If proceeding, prioritize integration planning to bridge Frankfurt HQ and San Francisco operations, and invest the $150K R&D improvement only if the required ~40% yield increase is realistically achievable
risks: Integration complexity due to geographic and cultural distance
Pipeline drugs may not perform as projected, reducing revenue upside
Competitive retaliation could erode market position
next_steps: Conduct full NPV valuation of the target including pipeline drug probabilities
Assess organizational readiness for cross-continental integration
Evaluate alternative targets and organic growth options before committing
Determine whether the R&D yield improvement is technically feasible before approving the $150K investment
